official_scope: climate change processes in the Earth system
design_notes: Expanded the 7 locked topics into 83 atomic concepts. The mission list topic includes 16 one-instrument concepts to ensure every listed platform/instrument has a home. Counts vary by topic density; no topics were merged or left as thin stubs.

topics.title: Electromagnetic radiation and remote sensing physics
topics.why_this_topic: Remote sensing interpretation depends on a clean foundation in the electromagnetic spectrum, blackbody emission, and how light interacts with the atmosphere and surfaces before any sensor or orbit is introduced.
topics.scope_note: Includes EMS regions, wave-particle properties, absorption/emission/scattering, blackbody laws (Wien, Stefan-Boltzmann), and spectroscopy; excludes instrument design, orbital mechanics, and full equilibrium temperature modeling.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic spectrum regions
concepts.description: Identify and order electromagnetic radiation regions by wavelength and frequency, and state which regions are used in common remote sensing instruments.

concepts.title: Wavelength-frequency conversion
concepts.description: Convert between wavelength and frequency using c = λν and compare photon energy across spectral bands.

concepts.title: Photon energy and Planck relation
concepts.description: Calculate photon energy with E = hν or E = hc/λ and relate photon energy to spectral region and detector requirements.

concepts.title: Blackbody emission curves
concepts.description: Interpret blackbody radiation curves for objects at different temperatures, including peak position and total emitted energy.

concepts.title: Wien's displacement law
concepts.description: Use Wien's displacement law to calculate peak emission wavelength from temperature or infer temperature from peak wavelength.

concepts.title: Stefan-Boltzmann law
concepts.description: Calculate total emitted power per unit area from an object's temperature using the Stefan-Boltzmann law, accounting for emissivity.

concepts.title: Atmospheric absorption and transmission windows
concepts.description: Identify atmospheric windows and absorption bands caused by water vapor, carbon dioxide, ozone, and other gases, and explain how they constrain sensor bands.

concepts.title: Rayleigh scattering and sky color
concepts.description: Explain Rayleigh scattering dominance at short wavelengths, its 1/λ⁴ dependence, and consequences for clear-sky remote sensing.

concepts.title: Mie scattering by aerosols and clouds
concepts.description: Distinguish Mie scattering from Rayleigh scattering by particle size and wavelength dependence, and predict its effect on cloud and aerosol imagery.

concepts.title: Non-selective scattering by cloud droplets
concepts.description: Describe non-selective scattering by water droplets and ice crystals when particle size greatly exceeds wavelength, and explain why clouds appear white.

concepts.title: Spectral reflectance signatures of surfaces
concepts.description: Interpret spectral reflectance curves for vegetation, soil, water, snow, and clouds to identify surface or atmospheric features in remotely sensed data.

topics.title: Sensor types and imaging fundamentals
topics.why_this_topic: The event explicitly tests active versus passive sensor distinctions and the physical basis of each instrument class, so a dedicated chapter prevents these from being buried under mission lists.
topics.scope_note: Includes active/passive sensing, optical/IR imagers, radiometers, LIDAR, space gravimetry, radar altimetry/precipitation radar/Doppler, and imaging fidelity/resolution metrics; excludes orbital parameters and mission-specific variable matchups.

concepts.title: Active vs passive sensors
concepts.description: Distinguish active sensors that emit their own energy from passive sensors that detect natural radiation, and classify common instruments accordingly.

concepts.title: Optical and infrared imaging radiometers
concepts.description: Describe how optical and infrared imagers measure reflected solar or emitted thermal radiation in discrete spectral bands and produce image pixels.

concepts.title: Passive microwave radiometry
concepts.description: Explain how passive microwave radiometers measure emitted microwave radiation to retrieve precipitation, soil moisture, and sea ice.

concepts.title: LIDAR backscatter profiling
concepts.description: Explain how LIDAR sends laser pulses and measures time-resolved backscatter to produce vertical profiles of aerosols and clouds.

concepts.title: Radar altimetry for sea surface height
concepts.description: Describe how radar altimeters transmit microwave pulses and measure round-trip time to retrieve sea surface height and wave height.

concepts.title: Precipitation radar and Doppler velocity retrieval
concepts.description: Explain how spaceborne precipitation radar measures radar reflectivity and Doppler shift to estimate precipitation rate and vertical motion.

concepts.title: Spaceborne gravimetry and mass change detection
concepts.description: Describe how precise tracking of satellite-to-satellite range detects gravity anomalies linked to terrestrial water storage and ice mass changes.

concepts.title: Spatial resolution and pixel footprint
concepts.description: Define spatial resolution and pixel footprint, and compare how pixel size affects detection of small features in remote sensing images.

concepts.title: Spectral resolution and bandwidth
concepts.description: Distinguish spectral resolution from spatial resolution, and explain how narrower bandwidths and hyperspectral sensors improve material discrimination.

concepts.title: Radiometric resolution and bit depth
concepts.description: Define radiometric resolution as sensitivity to signal differences and relate bit depth to the number of digital levels in an image.

concepts.title: Temporal resolution and revisit interval
concepts.description: Define temporal resolution as the repeat observation interval and explain tradeoffs between spatial resolution, swath width, and revisit frequency.

topics.title: Orbits and satellite platforms
topics.why_this_topic: Orbital geometry and platform choices determine temporal and spatial sampling, so students need a focused chapter on Kepler's laws and operational orbit types before applying specific missions.
topics.scope_note: Includes Kepler's laws, LEO/MEO/HEO/GEO/polar/sun-synchronous orbits, ground tracks, revisit time, and platform tradeoffs; excludes sensor electronics and retrieval algorithms.

concepts.title: Kepler's first law for satellite orbits
concepts.description: State that satellite orbits are ellipses with Earth at one focus, and identify perigee and apogee distances in an elliptical orbit.

concepts.title: Kepler's second law and orbital velocity
concepts.description: Use Kepler's second law to explain why a satellite moves faster near perigee and slower near apogee, sweeping equal areas in equal times.

concepts.title: Kepler's third law and orbital period
concepts.description: Calculate orbital period or semi-major axis using Kepler's third law and relate higher orbits to longer periods.

concepts.title: Orbital altitude and circular orbit speed
concepts.description: Calculate circular orbital speed and period for a given altitude above Earth, and infer altitude from period.

concepts.title: Geostationary orbit characteristics
concepts.description: Identify the altitude and period of a geostationary orbit, and explain why it provides continuous coverage of one hemisphere.

concepts.title: Low Earth orbit characteristics and tradeoffs
concepts.description: Describe typical LEO altitude, period, and spatial resolution advantages, and explain the limited revisit and coverage per orbit.

concepts.title: Polar and near-polar orbits
concepts.description: Explain how high-inclination polar orbits provide global coverage as Earth rotates beneath the satellite track.

concepts.title: Sun-synchronous orbit and consistent lighting
concepts.description: Describe how a sun-synchronous orbit precesses to maintain a nearly constant local solar time at each pass, improving data comparability.

concepts.title: Satellite ground tracks and swath coverage
concepts.description: Interpret ground track maps and explain how orbital motion and Earth rotation create successive tracks and gaps between swaths.

concepts.title: Revisit time and coverage tradeoffs
concepts.description: Evaluate satellite platform choices by trading off spatial resolution, swath width, and revisit time for monitoring climate variables.

topics.title: Major climate and Earth-observing satellite missions
topics.why_this_topic: The rules restrict satellite identification and context to a fixed list, so a dedicated mission chapter keeps instruments matched to the climate variables they measure without turning physics or energy balance into a dump category.
topics.scope_note: Covers only the listed satellites/instruments (MODIS Aqua, CALIPSO, CloudSat, GOES, Suomi NPP, GPM, PACE, JASON, GRACE, OCO-2, Aura, Tropomi/Sentinel-5P, ASTER/Terra, ECOSTRESS, CrIS, CERES) by cloud/precip, sea level/waves, GHG/trace gas/aerosol, temperature, and radiative flux context; excludes non-listed platforms and planetary/military systems.

concepts.title: MODIS on Aqua
concepts.description: Identify Aqua's Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer as a passive multispectral imager used for clouds, aerosols, sea surface temperature, and ocean color.

concepts.title: CALIPSO aerosol and cloud lidar
concepts.description: Identify CALIPSO as a polar-orbiting LIDAR mission that retrieves vertical profiles of aerosols and thin clouds using laser backscatter and depolarization.

concepts.title: CloudSat cloud profiling radar
concepts.description: Identify CloudSat as a millimeter-wave radar mission that measures cloud vertical structure, ice/liquid water content, and precipitation inside clouds.

concepts.title: GOES geostationary weather imaging
concepts.description: Identify GOES satellites as geostationary imagers providing continuous visible and infrared views for cloud tracking, convection, and water vapor.

concepts.title: Suomi NPP polar weather and climate observations
concepts.description: Identify Suomi NPP as a polar-orbiting platform carrying CrIS, ATMS, VIIRS, and CERES to support weather and climate data continuity.

concepts.title: GPM global precipitation measurement
concepts.description: Identify GPM as a precipitation-focused mission using a dual-frequency radar and radiometer to measure rain and snow globally.

concepts.title: PACE ocean color and aerosol mission
concepts.description: Identify PACE as a mission measuring hyperspectral ocean color, phytoplankton, and aerosol properties to study marine ecosystems and climate.

concepts.title: JASON radar altimetry for sea level
concepts.description: Identify JASON satellites as radar altimeters that measure global sea surface height, wave height, and ocean dynamic topography.

concepts.title: GRACE terrestrial water storage mission
concepts.description: Identify GRACE and GRACE-FO as twin-satellite gravimetry missions that track water storage anomalies, ice mass loss, and groundwater changes.

concepts.title: OCO-2 column carbon dioxide measurements
concepts.description: Identify OCO-2 as a polar-orbiting grating spectrometer that measures total column carbon dioxide for carbon cycle studies.

concepts.title: Aura atmospheric chemistry mission
concepts.description: Identify Aura as a polar mission measuring ozone, nitrogen dioxide, and other trace gases to monitor stratospheric and tropospheric chemistry.

concepts.title: Tropomi on Sentinel-5P trace gas columns
concepts.description: Identify TROPOMI as a hyperspectral imager on Sentinel-5P that provides high-resolution daily column measurements of NO2, SO2, ozone, and methane.

concepts.title: ASTER on Terra land surface and temperature
concepts.description: Identify ASTER as a high-spatial-resolution multispectral imager on Terra used for land surface temperature, emissivity, geology, and topography.

concepts.title: ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration from ISS
concepts.description: Identify ECOSTRESS as a thermal infrared radiometer on the ISS that retrieves evapotranspiration and plant water stress at high temporal cadence.

concepts.title: CrIS infrared sounding for temperature and moisture
concepts.description: Identify CrIS as a hyperspectral infrared sounder that retrieves vertical profiles of atmospheric temperature and water vapor.

concepts.title: CERES Earth radiation budget measurements
concepts.description: Identify CERES instruments as broadband radiometers that measure reflected solar and emitted thermal radiation to quantify Earth's energy balance.

topics.title: Satellite data interpretation and retrieval products
topics.why_this_topic: The written station format heavily tests reading imagery, vertical profiles, anomaly maps, and retrieval graphs, which is a separate skill from knowing mission hardware.
topics.scope_note: Includes interpreting cloud/precipitation/aerosol imagery, vertical profiles from CALIPSO/CloudSat, sea surface height and gravity maps, trace gas columns, temperature and radiative flux products; excludes mission background and pure orbital math.

concepts.title: Visible and infrared cloud imagery interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret cloud brightness, texture, and temperature from visible and infrared satellite imagery to identify cloud type, height, and potential convection.

concepts.title: Water vapor imagery and upper-level flow
concepts.description: Interpret water vapor channel imagery to identify dry air intrusions, jet streaks, and upper-level moisture transport.

concepts.title: CALIPSO vertical feature mask interpretation
concepts.description: Read CALIPSO attenuated backscatter and vertical feature mask plots to distinguish aerosol, cloud, and clear-air layers by altitude.

concepts.title: CloudSat radar reflectivity profile interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret CloudSat radar reflectivity vertical cross-sections to identify cloud top, base, precipitation, and mixed-phase regions.

concepts.title: GPM precipitation radar interpretation
concepts.description: Read GPM dual-frequency radar and radiometer products to infer precipitation intensity, phase, and vertical structure in storms.

concepts.title: Sea surface height anomaly maps
concepts.description: Interpret sea surface height anomaly fields from altimetry to identify warm and cold eddies, currents, and sea level rise patterns.

concepts.title: GRACE water storage anomaly maps
concepts.description: Interpret GRACE terrestrial water storage anomaly maps to identify regional drought, groundwater depletion, and ice mass loss signals.

concepts.title: Trace gas column and concentration maps
concepts.description: Interpret satellite column maps of NO2, SO2, CO2, and methane to identify pollution sources, transport, and seasonal variations.

concepts.title: Hyperspectral infrared temperature and moisture retrievals
concepts.description: Read temperature and dewpoint profiles from infrared and microwave sounder retrievals to diagnose atmospheric stability and moisture structure.

concepts.title: Aerosol optical depth retrieval and maps
concepts.description: Interpret aerosol optical depth maps to identify dust, smoke, and pollution events and estimate aerosol loading.

concepts.title: Ocean color and chlorophyll-a interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret ocean color products to estimate chlorophyll-a concentration, identify blooms, and relate phytoplankton to nutrient supply.

concepts.title: Vegetation indices and phenology from imagery
concepts.description: Calculate and interpret NDVI from red and near-infrared reflectance to assess vegetation health, greenness, and seasonal phenology.

topics.title: Climate processes, greenhouse gases, and Earth system cycles
topics.why_this_topic: The official climate processes section spans atmospheric chemistry, coupled ocean-atmosphere cycles, and ecosystem response, so it needs its own chapter rather than being mixed with energy balance calculations.
topics.scope_note: Includes GHG/aerosol distributions and drivers, ENSO, carbon and nitrogen cycles, climate effects on weather extremes, and ecological/vegetation impacts; excludes radiative transfer math and satellite hardware.

concepts.title: Greenhouse effect mechanism
concepts.description: Explain how greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, trapping heat in the lower atmosphere and warming the surface.

concepts.title: Carbon dioxide sources and sinks
concepts.description: Distinguish anthropogenic and natural CO2 sources, and identify land and ocean sinks that modulate atmospheric CO2 growth.

concepts.title: Methane sources and sinks
concepts.description: Identify major methane sources such as wetlands, agriculture, fossil fuels, and landfills, and explain its removal by atmospheric oxidation.

concepts.title: Aerosol direct and indirect climate effects
concepts.description: Distinguish aerosol direct radiative scattering/absorption from indirect effects on cloud albedo and lifetime, and state their net cooling influence.

concepts.title: Carbon cycle reservoirs and fluxes
concepts.description: Quantify major carbon reservoirs and fluxes among atmosphere, oceans, land biosphere, and geologic deposits, and identify human perturbation.

concepts.title: Anthropogenic nitrogen cycle changes
concepts.description: Describe how fertilizer production and fossil fuel combustion alter the nitrogen cycle, causing reactive nitrogen deposition and water quality impacts.

concepts.title: El Niño-Southern Oscillation cycle
concepts.description: Describe the coupled ocean-atmosphere ENSO cycle, including warm El Niño and cool La Niña phases and their global climate teleconnections.

concepts.title: Climate change and weather extremes
concepts.description: Assess how warming alters the frequency and intensity of heatwaves, heavy precipitation, drought, and storm-related flooding.

concepts.title: Vegetation phenology and climate response
concepts.description: Explain how satellite greenness indices reveal shifts in leaf-out, growing season length, and ecosystem productivity under climate change.

concepts.title: Ocean acidification from rising CO2
concepts.description: Explain how dissolved CO2 lowers ocean pH, affects carbonate chemistry, and stresses calcifying organisms.

concepts.title: Sea level rise contributors
concepts.description: Distinguish thermal expansion, glacier and ice sheet loss, and groundwater extraction as contributors to observed and projected sea level rise.

concepts.title: Permafrost thaw and carbon release
concepts.description: Explain how warming thaws permafrost, releases CO2 and methane, and creates a positive climate feedback.

topics.title: Earth's energy balance and radiative forcing
topics.why_this_topic: Quantitative equilibrium temperature modeling and radiative forcing/feedback questions form their own skill family, distinct from descriptive climate processes and sensor physics.
topics.scope_note: Includes albedo, cloud/aerosol effects, radiative forcing, feedbacks, applied blackbody Earth/Sun calculations, equilibrium temperature modeling, and heating/cooling rate trends; excludes spectral absorption line details and mission identification.

concepts.title: Planetary energy balance equation
concepts.description: Apply the principle that absorbed solar energy equals emitted terrestrial energy at equilibrium to compute global mean energy balance.

concepts.title: Solar constant and insolation geometry
concepts.description: Define the solar constant and calculate local insolation accounting for latitude, season, and time of day.

concepts.title: Planetary albedo and shortwave reflection
concepts.description: Define albedo as the fraction of incoming solar radiation reflected by Earth, and identify surface and cloud contributions to planetary albedo.

concepts.title: Effective radiating temperature
concepts.description: Calculate Earth's effective radiating temperature from absorbed solar flux and Stefan-Boltzmann law, and compare it to observed surface temperature.

concepts.title: Single-layer greenhouse surface temperature model
concepts.description: Use a single-layer atmosphere model to estimate surface temperature from incoming solar radiation and atmospheric longwave absorption/emission.

concepts.title: Radiative forcing definition and baseline
concepts.description: Define radiative forcing as the net change in downward energy flux at the tropopause due to a perturbation, and state its units and sign convention.

concepts.title: Radiative forcing of carbon dioxide
concepts.description: Calculate or estimate CO2 radiative forcing using logarithmic concentration dependence and explain why CO2 is the largest positive forcing.

concepts.title: Aerosol radiative forcing
concepts.description: Compare negative aerosol direct forcing from scattering sulfate aerosols with positive forcing from absorbing black carbon, and state net global aerosol forcing.

concepts.title: Cloud radiative effects on energy balance
concepts.description: Distinguish shortwave cooling from longwave warming by clouds, and predict net cloud forcing based on cloud altitude and optical thickness.

concepts.title: Climate feedbacks and gain
concepts.description: Identify water vapor, lapse rate, ice-albedo, and cloud feedbacks, and explain how positive feedbacks amplify initial temperature changes.

concepts.title: Equilibrium climate sensitivity
concepts.description: Define equilibrium climate sensitivity as the equilibrium global mean temperature change for a doubling of CO2, and compare canonical range estimates.
